flaws.evidence: DNS is not the primary failover mechanism; any DNS fallback uses a suitably low TTL and has resolver-caching limitations documented and tested.
The 99.95% target is an end-to-end service SLO, not the result of multiplying or averaging independent component availability claims.
Each tier has a disruption budget that permits controlled voluntary disruption... initially minAvailable: 5 for six replicas.
The HA standby is not used for reporting; it is not treated as a readable endpoint.
the BigQuery staleness limit is 15 minutes.

Restore duration is not assumed to be size-independent: restore and recovery targets are measured for the production database size and tested regularly.
Six replicas provide capacity above the 5,000-request-per-second peak

other_valid_list.issue: The draft's cross-region replica lag was not checked against the 5-minute RPO; the RPO was asserted without a measurement method.
The draft had no Datastream logical-decoding safeguards; replication slots and WAL growth could endanger primary storage.
The draft gave no account of how CDC meets the five-minute freshness objective across primary failover and replica promotion.
Regional recovery depended on capacity not provisioned in advance; the secondary GKE region needed pre-provisioned capacity and configuration.
The availability target had no defined treatment of planned maintenance, and the SLO boundaries and zone-loss versus regional-recovery responsibilities were undefined.
The RPO was not defined as an observed transaction-recovery measurement after promotion, so it could not be verified.

false_alarm_list.claim: Use at least `/20` for 30 nodes at the common `/24` pod-range-per-node allocation.
false_alarm_list.why: A `/20` contains only sixteen `/24` blocks, so it cannot cover 30 nodes under that allocation model.

other_valid_list.issue: The draft did not establish that Datastream logical decoding, slot/WAL retention, and BigQuery processing could meet the five-minute freshness commitment.
The draft did not establish that the asynchronous cross-region Cloud SQL replica could meet the five-minute RPO; lag and promotion behavior needed measurement.
Post-zone-loss capacity depended on autoscaler and pod-startup speed, but the draft did not show that capacity would arrive quickly enough.

flaws.evidence: DNS is not relied on for the 15-minute RTO; auxiliary DNS has a verified low TTL and documented resolver limitations.
End-to-end monthly availability SLO is 99.95%. Dependency and maintenance budgets will be tracked against it.
Initially use a PDB of minAvailable: 5 for a six-replica tier. Do not use 6 of 6 as routine upgrade policy.
The HA standby is not a reporting endpoint. Use a separately provisioned supported read replica.
The 15-minute staleness setting is absent from v4; section 7 sets a five-minute committed-change freshness target with a three-minute alert.
Use the Stable GKE release channel unless a required feature is unavailable.
Use required or preferred anti-affinity as appropriate, and verify constraints do not prevent rescheduling during zone failure.
Corruption recovery uses a tested, size-dependent restore procedure recording restore duration, achievable RPO, validation.
The initial target is six replicas if testing confirms approximately 800 requests/second per pod.
For the current maximum of 30 nodes at up to 110 pods per node, reserve at least /19 under the common allocation model.

false_alarm_list.claim: Use at least /20 for the pod range.
false_alarm_list.why: A /20 gives only 16 /24 per-node blocks, so it cannot support 30 nodes at 110 pods per node; the correct minimum under that model is /19.

false_alarm_list.claim: A /22 is not inherently insufficient for 30 nodes if GKE uses flexible pod CIDR sizing.
false_alarm_list.why: Under the default per-node allocation the /22 is insufficient, and flexible sizing does not change the arithmetic for the stated 110-pod nodes; the speaker's point is a qualification, not a valid defence of the draft, so it is at best misleading rather than a false criticism.

false_alarm_list.claim: Use required or preferred anti-affinity as appropriate.
false_alarm_list.why: Preferred anti-affinity gives no separation guarantee, and the final text does not say which form enforces node separation, so the placement requirement is left ambiguous.

other_valid_list.issue: Stated RPO of 5 minutes with cross-region Cloud SQL replication is asynchronous and cannot be guaranteed without measured lag bounds (raised in 12, 14, 16).
BigQuery merge must be idempotent using a durable event identity such as transaction/LSN, not just the row primary key (raised in 3, adopted in final section 7).
Datastream needs WAL retention bounding, slot monitoring and back-pressure protection so a stalled consumer cannot endanger primary storage (raised in 7, 9).
The stated 60% per zone and 90% after zone loss leave little headroom and do not establish that autoscaler reaction is fast enough (raised in 7, 8, 11).
Regional failover required the write endpoint switch, promotion and fencing sequence to be executable, not just a rehearsal assumption (raised in 14, 18, 20, 22).
The 30-node sizing did not state whether it included upgrade surge, failover capacity and growth (raised in 27, 33, 45).

The 800 requests/second per pod capacity was not validated: six replicas at that rate give 4,800 requests/second, below the 5,000 peak, and four replicas after zone loss give 3,200 (not raised by any speaker).

other_valid_list.issue: Validate Cloud NAT capacity, port exhaustion, and failure behavior, as well as regional quotas and autoscaler headroom; the draft did not establish these operational limits.
The five-minute RPO was not substantiated for asynchronous cross-region replication; measured replica lag, promotion testing, and recovery procedures are needed to assess whether it can be met.

Regional recovery needs coordinated write protection, database promotion, traffic shift, and rollback; treating these actions independently risks inconsistent writes or failed recovery.

flaws.evidence: Regional traffic shift uses the load balancer's health-based failover or traffic steering, not a 3,600-second DNS failover.
Individual managed-service targets do not automatically compose to the platform SLO; dependency failures consume the common error budget.
Each tier has a disruption budget... initially minAvailable: 5 for six replicas.
The HA standby is not used for reads. Analytics dashboards use a separately provisioned and sized Cloud SQL read replica.
A 15-minute BigQuery staleness limit conflicts with the five-minute committed-change target.
Use the GKE Regular release channel for production, with a tested maintenance policy.
Preferred hostname anti-affinity is used to reduce same-node concentration.
Restore objectives are size-dependent measured targets, not a claim of five minutes regardless of database size.
Six replicas provide capacity above the 5,000-request/second peak; this estimate is validated with load tests.
A /22 pod range cannot support 30 nodes at 110 pods/node

false_alarm_list.claim: The /22 has about 1,024 addresses versus 3,300 requested.
false_alarm_list.why: 3,300 is the pod count (30 nodes x 110 pods), not the address need. GKE reserves a /24 per node at 110 pods, so 30 nodes need about 7,680 addresses. The conclusion that /22 is too small is still correct.

other_valid_list.issue: Cloud NAT scaling, HA and port capacity were not validated in the original draft.
Post-zone-loss scaling to 90% utilisation was assumed without verifying autoscaler headroom or regional quotas.
Autoscaler headroom and regional quotas for post-zone-loss scaling were not validated.
The regional failover runbook did not coordinate write protection, Cloud SQL promotion and traffic shift, nor define rollback.
Cross-region replica lag was not monitored, so the 5-minute RPO was asserted rather than measured, and replica promotion was not validated.
Analytics read replica sizing, lag monitoring and degradation behaviour were not defined.
Datastream PostgreSQL logical-decoding prerequisites, replication-slot and WAL retention, and CDC impact on primary storage were not addressed.
